topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cellular transformation and cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how studying tumor viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and the experimental assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional classes of cancer genes and examine how mutations in key pathways such as Rb and p53 alter cell cycle control.

topics.label: Mechanisms, pathways, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how failures in DNA repair, replication, and mitotic segregation generate sequence or chromosomal instability and induce cellular stress.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations drives tumor progression and clinical cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with reading recommendations and a preview of the next session.
